evidence: Wikipedia's articles on TONTO and on Stevie Wonder: after Cecil and Margouleff's 'Zero Time' (1971), Wonder worked with them and TONTO on 'Music of My Mind' and 'Talking Book' (1972), 'Innervisions' (1973) and 'Fulfillingness' First Finale' (1974).

trackPair.whatToListenFor: 'Zero Time' is the instrument showing off: slow, spacey synthesizer pieces with no singer. On 'Living for the City' the same kind of sound is doing ordinary band jobs, playing bass lines and chords under a soul song. Listen for synthesizer parts that you might at first take for keyboards or horns.

explanation: TONTO was a homemade synthesizer the size of a room. Stevie Wonder heard an album its builders made and came to work with them, and for four albums in the early 1970s TONTO was part of his band: a one-off instrument shaping famous records because its owners came with it. It brought synthesizers that could play chords into Black popular music years before you could buy one in a shop, and through Wonder's albums it set an example for funk and R&B keyboard players through the 1970s.
